label: Filesystem
title: Filesystem
subtitle: Lets agents read, write, edit, and organise files and directories within the project workspace. This is the primary way agents create and manage output files — reports, code, data exports, and any other artefacts produced during a session.
whenToUse: Use when an agent needs to save its work to disk, read source files you have placed in the project folder, process documents, or build up a file-based output over multiple steps.

methods.name: Read File
methods.description: Reads the full text content of a file.

methods.name: Read Document
methods.description: Reads structured documents (PDF, DOCX, CSV, XLSX) and extracts text with metadata like headings and page numbers. An image is read too: a vision model describes it and transcribes the text in it.

methods.name: Read File Chunk
methods.description: Reads a specific byte range of a large file.

methods.name: Read Multiple Files
methods.description: Reads several files in one call and returns their contents together.

methods.name: Write File
methods.description: Creates or overwrites a file with the given content.

methods.name: Edit File
methods.description: Applies a targeted patch to an existing file — replaces a specific string with another.

methods.name: Append to File
methods.description: Adds content to the end of an existing file without overwriting it.

methods.name: List Directory
methods.description: Returns the files and subdirectories at a given path with metadata.

methods.name: Create Directory
methods.description: Creates a directory and any missing parent directories.

methods.name: Get File Info
methods.description: Returns metadata about a file without reading its content.

methods.name: Search Files
methods.description: Searches file contents using a regex pattern and returns matching lines with file paths and line numbers.

mediaCaption: A filesystem Write File action card showing the file path and a preview of the content the agent is saving
tips: Use Edit File rather than Write File when modifying an existing file — it is faster and avoids accidentally overwriting unrelated content.
Search Files is very useful for agents doing code analysis across a multi-file codebase.
Writing or editing a file shows the change as a diff in the chat — a new file as an added file, an edit as the replaced lines — so you can see exactly what changed at a glance.
